name: Filmstrip
description: Black box, yellow active word.
as_you_speak: The spoken word sits in a box
best_for: throwback, high-contrast looks in yellow, black and italic
when_to_use: Use Filmstrip for a classic, readable subtitle bar. Words sit on a black box and the active word turns yellow, up to five at a time. It suits interviews, podcasts, documentary-style clips and longer explanations where viewers need whole phrases on screen.
skip_when: Skip it when you want the caption to be part of the art; the black bar is functional rather than decorative.

name: Dolly
description: Small setup, big keyword slides forward.
as_you_speak: Words spring in as they are spoken
best_for: throwback, high-contrast looks in yellow, black and italic
when_to_use: Use Dolly for tips and listicles where each line has one keyword: a small setup phrase, then the big keyword slides forward as you say it. Two words per group in Montserrat ExtraBold keep the pace brisk, which suits educators, coaches and how-to clips.
skip_when: Skip it when sentences have no clear keyword. The slide-forward move loses its meaning when every word gets it.

name: Searchlight
description: A light band scans across the words.
as_you_speak: A light sweep follows the voice
best_for: throwback, high-contrast looks in yellow, black and italic
